page: OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is a dedicated cloud GPU instance provisioned via KVM virtualization within the Cloud GPU family. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor featuring 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Compute resources are paired with 28 GB of system memory, providing a generous 7 GB allocation per vCPU core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA RTX 5000 GPU based on the Turing architecture, equipped with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage is bundled locally with a 400 GB SSD, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

Benchmark results highlight strong specialized acceleration contrasted with moderate host compute throughput. The Turing GPU demonstrates top-tier efficiency for small and medium language model execution, reaching 10592.7 prompt tokens per second and 386.55 text generation tokens per second on a 135M model, alongside 1854.84 prompt tokens per second and 67.41 generation tokens per second on a 7B model. Host compute capabilities align with mid-tier profiles, recording a single-core Geekbench score of 1437.0 and a multi-core score of 4430.0. Memory bandwidth delivers solid cached reads at 353.33 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write speeds decline to 19.59 GB/sec.

Resource allocation presents clear architectural tradeoffs. The dedicated single-threaded vCPU mapping ensures stable compute performance without hyperthreading contention, while the 16 GB VRAM envelope bounds model execution sizes, precluding large 70B parameter models without distributed offloading. The combination of dedicated host cores, ample system RAM, bundled local SSD space, and hardware acceleration delivers efficient resource density for targeted graphics and machine learning tasks. OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is primarily fit for small-to-medium LLM inference, computer vision processing, 3D visualization, video transcoding pipelines, and accelerated development environments.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is a cloud GPU server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor at 3.3 GHz, 28 GB of RAM, and a bundled 400 GB local SSD. Graphical and tensor acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA RTX 5000 Turing GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, supported by a 2 Gbps network link. In benchmark testing, the instance achieves top-tier throughput in small and medium LLM inference, reaching over 10,000 tokens per second for prompt evaluation on 135M models and solid text generation across 7B architectures. Host compute and memory bandwidth exhibit balanced middle-tier baseline behavior across standard CPU workloads. While constrained by its 16 GB VRAM limit for very large model execution, the server provides cost-effective resource density for small-to-midsize deep learning inference, image processing, 3D rendering, and GPU-accelerated staging workloads.
